# Clunk

> Clunk is an engine-aware quality gate for real 2D, Sprite, Spine, animation, and 3D assets.
> It keeps structural evidence, engine import/runtime evidence, and player-facing review separate.
> 한국어: 실제 2D·Sprite·Spine·애니메이션·3D 에셋을 목표 엔진에 대조하되 화면 판정과 분리하는 품질 게이트입니다.

Status: private pilot (Korea first). Billing is a working demo ledger, not a payment provider.

Clunk HTTP MCP: shipped at `/api/mcp`. It is Clunk's own streamable HTTP route, authenticated with a
workspace-scoped `Authorization: Bearer clunk_live_...` key issued from `/agents`. The route can
inspect uploaded base64 asset bundles, store verified v2 evidence, and append frame manifests to
workspace collaboration threads. It never reads a caller's local absolute path over HTTP. The
local stdio MCP remains the correct transport for files that only exist on the caller's machine.
The Sites access policy still controls whether an external client can reach the published URL.

### Browser WebMCP

The site also contains a read-only WebMCP bridge. When the browser exposes the current imperative
API at `document.modelContext`, Clunk registers `clunk_connection_check` and
`clunk_product_capabilities`; older experimental browsers may expose the deprecated
`navigator.modelContext` fallback. The page visibly reports `REGISTERED`, `UNAVAILABLE`, or
`ERROR`. These browser tools describe the HTTP endpoint and contract boundary only: they do not
read a caller's local path, run `clunk_optimize`, or promote `structural=PASS` to
`visualRuntime=PASS`, `playerFacing=PASS`, or human approval. Authenticated asset inspection and
`initialize`/`tools/list` remain on the `/agents` HTTP MCP connection flow.

Client setup is generated per client from `/agents` after sign-in: Claude Code receives a
`claude mcp add --transport http clunk <endpoint> --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>"` command;
Codex receives `codex mcp add clunk --url <endpoint> --bearer-token-env-var CLUNK_API_KEY` plus a
PowerShell environment assignment; GitHub Copilot receives `copilot mcp add --transport http` with
the Authorization header; Cursor and Claude Desktop receive `mcpServers` JSON; VS Code receives
`servers` JSON. These are client-specific forms, not a Polyfork command. The copied key is shown once.

## What Clunk actually does

- Parses real GLB and glTF 2.0 bytes. No screenshot, no fixture, no mock metric.
- Records `inputHash` (SHA-256 of the input bytes), `coreBuildId`, `ruleSetId`, `ruleSetVersion`
  and `resultDigest` for every run.
- `clunk.asset-evidence-ref.v1` links a frame manifest to a real source inspection with
  `inputHash`, `resultDigest`, `byteLength`, `coreBuildId`, `ruleSetId`, `ruleSetVersion`,
  `profileId` for CURRENT evidence, optional `analysisId`, and `freshness: CURRENT|STALE|UNKNOWN`.
  Every fresh HF `assetInspections[]` entry also requires `inspectionRunId` and `targetProfileId`;
  CURRENT `profileId` identifies the concrete Core profile and is required. Legacy STALE/UNKNOWN
  refs may omit it. `CURRENT` is a
  producer-supplied current reinspection; `STALE EVIDENCE · NOT CURRENT APPROVAL` and
  `FRESHNESS UNKNOWN · NOT CURRENT APPROVAL` never promote `reviewStatus`, `visualRuntime`,
  or `playerFacing`. A malformed ref or evidence input-hash mismatch is `INVALID` and is
  rejected by normalization/API. The dashboard displays the full input hash, result digest,
  byte length, rule set, build, and freshness beside the linked asset inspection.
- Evaluates 17 rules across 6 categories (format, scene, geometry, materials, textures, runtime).
  Rule set: `clunk-game-ready-v1` v`1.0.0`. Ready score threshold: 90.
- Every finding carries `ruleId`, `severity`, `path`, `observed` and `threshold`.
- Optimizes with an allowlist only, then re-inspects the produced artifact from scratch.

## Verdicts

- `준비 완료` (ready): no blocking finding, declared policy satisfied.
- `조건부 준비` (conditional): no hard blocker, warnings remain that lossless cleanup cannot fix.
- `차단됨` (blocked): at least one ERROR or CRITICAL finding remains.

## MCP server

### Clunk-owned remote HTTP

Open `/agents`, sign in, click `Clunk 연결 키 만들기`, and use the generated client block. The
canonical endpoint is the same-origin `/api/mcp` route (production:
`https://clunk.honna1.chatgpt.site/api/mcp`). The key is displayed once and can be revoked from the
same page. A minimal request is:

```http
POST /api/mcp
Authorization: Bearer clunk_live_<issued-key>
Content-Type: application/json

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18"}}
```

The remote HTTP `tools/list` surface contains exactly 7 tools: `clunk_connection_check`, `clunk_asset_inspect`,
`clunk_asset_validate`, `clunk_asset_inspection_evidence`, `clunk_collaboration_append`,
`clunk_scene_review`, and `clunk_sprite_sheet_review`.
`clunk_asset_inspect` and `clunk_asset_validate` accept the existing
`clunk.asset-inspection-request.v1|v2` shape with `bytesBase64` or `files[]`; raw bytes are not
persisted. `clunk_asset_inspection_evidence` accepts a normalized
`clunk.asset-inspection-evidence.v2` `CONTRACT_FIXTURE`; `PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE` still requires
locally verified capture bytes through the CLI or local MCP. `clunk_collaboration_append` accepts
`threadId`, `evidenceMode: append|replace`, and a normalized frame manifest. `clunk_scene_review`
normalizes shipped frame metadata and `clunk_sprite_sheet_review` normalizes the declared Pixi
manifest; HTTP remains `DECLARED_METADATA_ONLY` and never rehashes local paths. It never promotes
`reviewStatus`, `visualRuntime`, `playerFacing`, or `humanDecision`.

The local stdio surface contains 7 advertised tools, including `clunk_inspect`, `clunk_optimize`,
`clunk_asset_author`, `clunk_scene_review`, and `clunk_sprite_sheet_review`. Legacy
`clunk_validate` and `clunk_passport` calls remain backward-compatible handlers. These catalogs are
intentionally different: HTTP agents upload bytes/evidence, while local stdio is the only path
that can read a local absolute path or write an authoring output in the caller's workspace.
For HTTP `clunk_asset_inspect` and `clunk_asset_validate`, use an engine-aware
`targetProfileId` such as `harvest-frontier-web-three`; local stdio names `pc`, `web`, and
`mobile` are not valid HTTP target profile IDs. Local sprite review runs the exact RGBA audit and
returns `LOCAL_CLI_BYTE_REHASH`; local scene review preserves `visualRuntime=GAP`,
`playerFacing=NOT_EVALUATED`, and `humanDecision=NOT_EVALUATED` until separate capture and human evidence exists.

### Local stdio fallback

Transport: stdio, JSON-RPC. `initialize` returns protocolVersion `2025-06-18` and
serverInfo `{ "name": "clunk", "version": "0.1.0" }`. Works with any MCP capable agent.

Client config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clunk": {
      "command": "cmd.exe",
      "args": ["/d", "/s", "/c", "call", "npm.cmd", "run", "--silent", "mcp"],
      "cwd": "<CLUNK_ROOT>"
    }
  }
}
```

Tools returned by local stdio `tools/list`:

- `clunk_inspect` - Inspect a real GLB/GLTF using Clunk Core.
  input: `path` (required), `profile` (`web` | `mobile` | `pc`).
  output: inspection report, `inputHash`, `resultDigest`.
- `clunk_optimize` - Apply only Clunk's allowlisted render-safe and metadata-only operations
  and write a new artifact.
  input: `path` (required), `outputPath`, `profile`.
  output: applied `operations`, `outputHash`, path of the new file.
- `clunk_passport` - Create a Passport by freshly inspecting source and output artifacts.
  input: `sourcePath` (required), `outputPath` (required), `profile`.
  output: Passport linking both hashes and both inspection digests.
- `clunk_asset_inspect` - Inspect a real 2D, Sprite, Spine, animation, or 3D asset against an
  engine-aware target profile.
  input: `path` (required), `targetProfileId` (required), optional `assetKind`, `runId`.
  output: canonical `AssetEvidence` with bytes/structure/policy/import/runtime/device stages,
  `qualityWarnings[]`, source hash, and `productionReady`. Missing runners remain
  `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`; no runtime PASS is inferred.
- `clunk_asset_inspection_evidence` - Build `clunk.asset-inspection-evidence.v2` from a real
  asset. `evidenceKind` is `CONTRACT_FIXTURE` or `PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE`; the latter requires
  local capture-byte verification and an explicit human decision.
- `clunk_asset_author` - Author real 2D, Sprite, Spine, animation, or 3D bytes through a
  registered adapter and reopen the result through AssetOps.
- `clunk_scene_review` - Review a normalized player-facing scene manifest while keeping runtime
  evidence and human review separate from static asset results.
- `clunk_sprite_sheet_review` - Rehash a local RGBA sprite sheet and validate the Pixi sprite
  contract, motion, clipping, alpha spill, border, silhouette, runtime-size, and provenance gates.

`clunk_validate` and `clunk_passport` remain backward-compatible calls in the local server but
are not advertised by the current seven-tool catalog.

Harvest Frontier acceptance fixture:
`examples/frame-manifest/harvest-frontier-m123-camera-review.example.json`.
Validate it with `npm.cmd exec -- tsx tests/harvest-frontier-m123-acceptance.test.ts`.
The fixture records real M123 WebGPU/WebGL2 candidate hashes, numeric camera checks, and the
canonical tractor structural evidence; it intentionally reports `reviewStatus=NOT_EVALUATED`,
`visualRuntime=GAP`, `playerFacing=NOT_EVALUATED`, and pending human review.

Typical agent loop: `initialize` -> `tools/list` -> `clunk_asset_inspect` or
`clunk_sprite_sheet_review` -> (if fixable) `clunk_optimize` -> fresh evidence review.

## CLI

```bash
npm run clunk -- inspect <asset.glb> --profile pc
npm run clunk -- validate <asset.glb> --profile web
npm run clunk -- optimize <asset.glb> --out <output.glb>
npm run clunk -- passport <source.glb> <optimized.glb>
```

`validate` exits with code 2 when the asset does not satisfy the declared policy, so it can be
used directly as a CI gate. All commands print one JSON envelope on stdout.

Watch mode re-inspects files on change and keeps a bytes/sha256/score manifest fresh, with an
optional `--ref <commit>` stamp, so Clunk can sit inside a pipeline instead of being invoked
per event:

```bash
npm run clunk -- watch <paths...> --profile-file <profile.json> --manifest out.json --ref <commit>
```

## Texture set audit

Tiling/terrain textures intentionally live outside GLBs, so they get their own input type:
`scripts/texture-audit.mjs <config.json> [--strict]`. Per texture and usage density (m/tile) it
reports mip readability per camera-distance band (grade A-D with a numeric prescription), tile
seam verdicts (SEAMLESS / SOFT-SEAM / MASKED / VISIBLE-SEAM with placement-context exposure),
and mip-inclusive GPU memory versus a budget. `--strict` exits 2 on exposed seams, gameplay-band
D grades, or a blown budget (checks selectable via `strictChecks`). Calibrated against a real
game team's visual ground truth (8/8 agreement); see docs/texture-audit.ko.md.

The stable external wrapper is `npm.cmd run asset:readability -- --config <config.json>
--format json --strict` and returns schema `clunk.texture-audit.v1`. This is a texture policy
result, not an engine import/runtime or player-facing result. Non-blocking texture follow-ups
are also representable as `qualityWarnings[]` with `status: "NON_BLOCKING"`; they do not erase
or promote a hard validation result. `evaluationProfile` supports `id`, `renderer`,
`viewport`, `camera`, `distanceBands[{id,distanceM,requiredGrade}]`, `resolutionPolicy`,
`repetition`, and `banding`. The report emits `measurementScope: "texture-only"`,
`visualRuntime: "NOT_EVALUATED"`, per-band grades/transitions, source resolution, and
`repetition.status: "DECLARED_ONLY"`; it does not claim repetition visibility from a texture-only
input. `strictChecks` may independently opt into `seam`, `memory`, `readability`, `banding`, or
`resolution` without changing the default HF seam/memory gate.

Measured world context is also supported without turning a texture-only result into a runtime
approval: `evaluationProfile.worldScale` and per-texture `sceneRole`, `surfaceRole`, and
`worldScale` record the HF soil/grass/ridge scale. Each usage returns `worldScaleMPerTile` beside
`mPerTile`. These fields are prescriptions for shipped-frame follow-up, not evidence that the
material reads correctly in a browser or game.

The target-aware local command returns the same Core envelope as `clunk_asset_inspect`:

```powershell
npm.cmd run asset:inspect -- --path <asset> --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --format json
```

Exit `0` means every required stage was actually evidenced and READY; exit `3` means the target
contract rejects the format/kind; exit `4` means an engine/runtime stage is unavailable. A
successful static analyzer does not make `productionReady` true when import/runtime is absent.

## Profile-aware generation

The current authoring adapters are deterministic and real, with engine runtime kept as a separate gate:

- Request schema: `clunk.asset-generation-request.v1`.
- Result schema: `clunk.asset-generation-result.v1`.
- Command: `npm.cmd run asset:generate -- --factory <factory.mjs> --target-profile <profile> --recipe-id threejs-factory-v1 --output-directory <separate-dir>`.
- The adapters export a texture-free three.js factory, PNG sprite sheet, atlas page, Spine JSON bundle, or animation GLB to a separate output directory, record source/request/recipe hashes, and reopen the output with the same target profile.
- `outputReopen: pass` proves fresh parsing of the generated bytes only. Missing engine import/runtime remains `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE` and exit `4`.
- 2D image, Sprite atlas, Spine JSON, and animation authoring adapters are shipped for the
  local verified rail. They write real PNG/atlas/JSON/GLB bytes into a separate output directory,
  then reopen those bytes through AssetOps. Their engine import/runtime stage still returns
  `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE` until a real runner is supplied. Binary Spine `.skel` authoring and
  licensed Spine export parity remain unavailable; an unregistered recipe returns
  `AUTHORING_UNAVAILABLE` and writes no pretend files.
- A procedural source does not get a fabricated Passport. A real source/output pair must be freshly inspected with `clunk_passport` to link both hashes and inspection digests.

## 2D and engine target contract

Core analyzers accept real PNG/JPG/WebP bytes, Sprite atlas text, Spine JSON projects, and glTF
animation clips in addition to GLB/glTF models. Built-in target declarations cover Web/Three.js,
Godot 4, Unity, Unreal, Web/Three.js Mobile, Android, and iOS. They describe format, coordinate,
texture, animation, and device constraints. An engine import/runtime/device stage that was not
actually invoked remains `notRun`, `environmentUnavailable`, or `unsupported`; it cannot become
READY by declaration alone.

Portrait/UI raster readability is shipped as a separate contract. The stable command is:

```powershell
npm.cmd run asset:ui-readability -- --config examples/ui-readability/harvest-frontier.portraits.json --format json --strict
```

It returns `clunk.ui-readability.v1` with `status: PASS` or `FAIL`, `capability: shipped`,
`inputHash`, `configHash`, per-image raster metrics at `renderPx`, and exit `0` or `2` under
`--strict`. Unsupported image formats or an unavailable decoder remain `status: UNAVAILABLE`
with exit `4`. The auditor measures the actual 46px HUD raster when `renderPx: 46` is declared;
it does not execute an engine import/runtime or player-facing frame. `assetAudit.status` and
`playerFacing.status` therefore remain `NOT_EVALUATED` and must not be promoted to READY.

## Asset inspection evidence v2

The committed v2 evidence contract is `clunk.asset-inspection-evidence.v2`. It is separate from
`clunk.frame-manifest.v1` and preserves the structural inspection identity: `inputHash`,
`resultDigest`, `byteLength`, `coreBuildId`, `ruleSetId`, `ruleSetVersion`, `profileId`,
`profileHash`, and `inspectionRunId`. `source` repeats the input bytes/hash;
`sourceOutputRelation` is `SOURCE`, `OUTPUT`, or `SOURCE_OUTPUT_PAIR` and never overwrites the
source artifact.

`evidenceKind` has two explicit lanes:

- `CONTRACT_FIXTURE`: structural/technical evidence only. It normalizes to
  `visualRuntime: GAP`, `playerFacing: NOT_EVALUATED`, `humanDecision: NOT_EVALUATED`, and
  `reviewStatus: NOT_EVALUATED`.
- `PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE`: requires hashed screenshot/frame evidence with bytes. It may retain
  `humanDecision: NO_GO`, `PASS_WITH_FOLLOW_UP`, or `PASS`, but a numeric score never supplies a
  human decision. A capture without a decision remains `reviewStatus: PENDING`.

The envelope includes structured `findings[]` (`code`, `severity`, `observed`, `threshold`,
`rationale`, `recommendation`, `ownership`, and `enforcement`) and optional `audioEvidence[]`
with queue id, channels, sample rate, duration, RMS/peak, L/R balance, side/mid, and clipping
metadata. `byteVerification` records the source and every capture/audio SHA and byte count with
`verified: true`; CLI uses `LOCAL_CLI_READ`, MCP uses `MCP_READ`, and the authenticated API does
not attest local paths. `qualityPolicy` is explicit and per rule: `OFF`, `ADVISORY`, or `BLOCKING`. Advisory
violations make readiness `conditional`; blocking violations make it `blocked`; neither changes
the legacy structural score. `textureCount: 0`, missing normals/UVs, non-unit scales, and bounds
remain observations until asset/runtime ownership is supplied.

Stable local CLI:

```powershell
npm.cmd run asset:evidence -- inspect <asset.glb> --profile-file <profile.json> `
  --evidence-kind CONTRACT_FIXTURE --inspection-run-id <run-id> --out evidence.json
npm.cmd run asset:evidence -- validate <asset.glb> --profile-file <profile.json> `
  --evidence-kind CONTRACT_FIXTURE --required
npm.cmd run asset:evidence -- normalize --input evidence.json
```

The CLI exits `0` for a valid envelope and `2` for invalid input or a required validation
failure. `--capture <path>` may be repeated for `PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE`; it reads each local file
and records absolute path, bytes, SHA-256, renderer, viewport, camera/source-tree hashes,
console counts (`--console-errors`, `--console-warnings`), and `--shipped-path`. `--audio <path>`
plus `--audio-metadata '<json>'` records the audio lane. The CLI writes with exclusive create,
so `--out` never overwrites an existing evidence file. The read-only MCP equivalent is
`clunk_asset_inspection_evidence` or `clunk_inspect`/`clunk_validate` with `evidenceFormat: "v2"`;
the authenticated validation endpoint is `POST /api/asset-inspection-evidence` for
`CONTRACT_FIXTURE` envelopes only. CLI and MCP read the actual asset/capture bytes and emit
`byteVerification`; the API cannot read a caller's local path and rejects
`PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE` with HTTP 422. All surfaces validate and normalize evidence; none
promotes visual status or replaces collaboration thread state.

## Authenticated collaboration

Workspace members can store and read asset-linked notes with `inputHash`, custom/base profile,
rule-set, and separate `assetAudit` / `visualRuntime` states:

- `GET /api/collaboration/threads`
- `POST /api/collaboration/threads`
- `GET /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId`
- `POST /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId/messages`
- `PATCH /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId`
- `GET/POST /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId/evidence`

`SCENE_GAP` means Clunk's static asset audit passed but the shipped scene or player-facing review
still has a gap. This contract requires host authentication and workspace scoping. A screenshot
or frame manifest is optional on thread/message POST and uses `clunk.frame-manifest.v1`; it is
evidence only and keeps `reviewStatus: NOT_EVALUATED`.
Normalized manifests also carry `visualRuntime: GAP` and `playerFacing: NOT_EVALUATED` by default;
the current v1 evidence contract rejects promotion of those fields, so a status snapshot or human
review cannot be smuggled in as a frame upload.
The collaboration status also exposes a machine-readable `readinessReason`: `STATIC_AUDIT_NOT_RUN`,
`STATIC_AUDIT_FAILED`, `STATIC_AUDIT_BLOCKED`, `VISUAL_RUNTIME_NOT_EVALUATED`,
`ENGINE_ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, `PLAYER_FACING_REVIEW_INPUT_INCOMPLETE`, `PLAYER_FACING_SCENE_GAP`, `VISUAL_RUNTIME_BLOCKED`, or
`PLAYER_FACING_REVIEW_PASS`. `visualRuntime` accepts `NOT_RUN|PASS|GAP|BLOCKED|UNAVAILABLE`;
`UNAVAILABLE` means the requested engine/device runner is not shipped and is never a PASS. Static
PASS plus visual pending/GAP/UNAVAILABLE is `conditional`; only an explicit runtime PASS with human
review is `ready`; hard blockers are `blocked`.
Frame entries may also carry `sha256`, `viewport`, `renderer`, `shippedPath`, and
`console: { errors, warnings }` so a packaged capture's provenance and browser/runtime smoke
signal stay attached to the frame without becoming a player-facing verdict. They may also carry
`distanceBandId` and `distanceM`; linked `assetInspections[].frameIds` then connect a source asset
or procedural origin to the same renderer/viewport/distance evidence.
`runtimeChecks[]` is the separate numeric layer: each item has `id`, `kind`, `status`, optional
renderer/evidencePath/frameIds, and a `checks` object such as `poseFocusId`,
`poseFocusOnScreen`, `poseFocusCoverage`, and `poseFocusLensInside`. A numeric `PASS` is not a
human visual review and does not change `reviewStatus` or `visualRuntime`.
The evidence-only endpoint accepts the same normalized manifest with `evidenceMode: "append"` or
`"replace"`; it requires the same host authentication and workspace scope as thread writes and
does not change the thread status snapshot.

The current live D1 HF-M94 evidence is not a placeholder. Its actual collaboration row has
`inputHash` `a8500559f6137a4ab35c3b7adb3a95e2d323198c11a0be00340ea3940db3552f`,
`runId` `HF-M94-packaged-r01`, `sourceCommit` `3e3e343`,
`frameSourceCommit` `d3d56464`, frame id `hf-m94-packaged-r01-03-game-nohud`,
frame bytes `2821399`, and frame SHA-256
`5978400B0DD77A5ED90EDE70617726B0DB838A5892075BDDD18DA5CCE0F58E15`.
It has exactly five scene gaps (`distant-terrain-band`, `simplified-hedge-rock-silhouettes`,
`tiny-soft-signage`, `dealer-camera-composition`, `dialogue-composition`) and six
non-blocking prescriptions: grass close layer D at 15m, dirt path C at 15m, tilled soil D at
15m, wider grass A/B, ridge/plaster/roof detail strengthening, and wood SOFT-SEAM.
The stored default boundary is `reviewStatus: NOT_EVALUATED`, `visualRuntime: GAP`, and
`playerFacing: NOT_EVALUATED`.

A manifest is reviewable only when the submitted set includes a no-HUD shipped baseline plus
dealer approach/counter, dialogue NPC/camera, and distant terrain/vegetation/sign frames from
the same source/build lineage. Each frame must carry `runId`, `sourceCommit`,
`frameSourceCommit`, id/path, sha256, bytes, renderer, viewport, `shippedPath`, `hud`, console
counts, and scene-gap `frameIds`. A normalized capture is reviewable evidence; it is not a visual
approval. Closing a scene gap requires an explicit human visual review of a fresh shipped-path
capture that clears every linked gap. Numeric or camera-clearance PASS alone never changes
`reviewStatus: NOT_EVALUATED` or `playerFacing: NOT_EVALUATED`.

HF's actual M94 texture follow-ups are non-blocking prescriptions linked to
`hf-m94-packaged-r01-03-game-nohud`: grass-meadow D at 15m -> secondary macro/detail or broken
tiling; dirt-path C at 15m -> edge blend/macro variation or distance material; soil-tilled D at
15m -> furrow/secondary structure or LOD detail; wood-planks C -> UV seam/scale and roughness/
normal breakup; plaster C -> macro breakup and distance-aware material; roof tiles B -> retain
as P2 observation until the corrected dealer/market camera proves loss. These are prescriptions,
not hard validation failures and never justify blanket resolution upscaling.

The stable thread POST body schema template below is intentionally not that stored evidence;
replace every `<...>` value with the next real capture:

```json
{
  "subject": "HF M84 no-HUD scene gaps",
    "inputHash": "<64 lowercase hex from the real Clunk result>",
    "evidenceMode": "replace",
  "status": {
    "assetAudit": "PASS",
    "visualRuntime": "GAP",
    "profileId": "harvest-frontier-runtime-v1",
    "baseProfileId": "pc",
    "ruleSetId": "harvest-frontier-runtime-v1",
    "inputHash": "<same 64-hex value>"
  },
  "evidence": {
    "schema": "clunk.frame-manifest.v1",
    "runId": "<RUN_ID>",
  "sourceProject": "<PROJECT>",
  "sourceCommit": "<SOURCE_COMMIT>",
  "reviewStatus": "NOT_EVALUATED",
  "visualRuntime": "GAP",
  "playerFacing": "NOT_EVALUATED",
  "frames": [{
      "id": "<FRAME_ID>",
      "path": "<FRAME_PATH>",
      "renderer": "<RENDERER>",
      "hud": "off",
      "distanceBandId": "gameplay",
      "distanceM": 15,
      "bytes": 2821399,
      "frameSourceCommit": "<FRAME_SOURCE_COMMIT>",
      "shippedPath": true,
      "console": { "errors": 0, "warnings": 0 },
      "viewport": { "width": 2560, "height": 1440, "dpr": 1 }
    }],
    "runtimeChecks": [{
      "id": "<RUNTIME_CHECK_ID>",
      "kind": "dialogue-camera",
      "status": "PASS",
      "renderer": "<RENDERER>",
      "evidencePath": "<RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_JSON>",
      "frameIds": ["<FRAME_ID>"],
      "checks": { "poseFocusId": "<NPC_ID>", "poseFocusOnScreen": true,
        "poseFocusCoverage": 0.01517, "poseFocusLensInside": false }
    }],
    "sceneGaps": [{
      "id": "terrain-seams",
      "severity": "major",
      "category": "environment",
      "note": "Describe the visible gap and its player-facing impact.",
      "ownership": "scene",
      "affectedScene": "farm-long-shot",
      "affectedAssetIds": ["<ASSET_INSPECTION_ID>"],
      "nextStep": "Describe the next shipped-path capture/action.",
      "evidence": { "path": "<FRAME_OR_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_PATH>", "sha256": "<64_HEX_SHA256>", "bytes": 1 },
      "frameIds": ["<FRAME_ID>"]
    }],
    "prescriptions": [{
      "id": "<PRESCRIPTION_ID>",
      "kind": "<KIND>",
      "status": "NON_BLOCKING",
      "priority": "P1",
      "observation": "<OBSERVATION>",
      "action": "<ACTION>",
      "frameIds": ["<FRAME_ID>"]
    }],
    "assetInspections": [{
      "id": "<ASSET_INSPECTION_ID>",
      "sourcePath": "<SOURCE_ASSET_PATH>",
      "inputHash": "<64_HEX_ASSET_HASH>",
      "assetKind": "3d-model",
      "targetProfileId": "<TARGET_PROFILE_ID>",
      "inspectionRunId": "<INSPECTION_RUN_ID>",
      "evidenceStatus": "ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE",
      "productionReady": false,
      "origin": "file",
      "ownership": "unknown",
      "runtimeUsage": "UNKNOWN",
      "frameIds": ["<FRAME_ID>"],
      "qualityWarningIds": ["<QUALITY_WARNING_ID>"],
      "numericContract": {
        "status": "PASS", "valid": true, "score": 100, "threshold": 90,
        "hardBlockerCount": 0, "findingIds": ["<INFO_FINDING_ID>"],
        "observations": { "drawCallCount": 88, "bounds": "<OBSERVED_BOUNDS>" }
      }
    }]
  }
}
```

`GET /api/collaboration/threads` returns `threads[]` with `status` and normalized `evidence`;
`GET /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId` returns the same thread plus `messages[]`, each with
its own optional `evidence`. A successful thread POST returns `201` and `{ "ok": true,
"thread": { "id": "...", "status": { ... }, "evidence": { ... } } }`. A malformed manifest is
rejected with `400`; optional `prescriptions[]` entries are explicitly `NON_BLOCKING` and carry
an observation plus next action. Unsupported or unknown player-facing evaluation is never
converted to PASS.

Evidence writes require an explicit merge rule. `evidenceMode: "replace"` treats the incoming
manifest as the complete snapshot and removes omitted frames, scene gaps, and prescriptions.
`evidenceMode: "append"` keeps existing items, appends new stable IDs, and upserts an incoming
item when its ID already exists; it requires the same `runId` and `sourceProject` and rejects a
cross-run merge with `409`. Use `PATCH /api/collaboration/threads/:threadId` for the canonical
thread snapshot. A message POST may also carry the same mode and evidence; the merged snapshot
is stored on both the message and thread. Omitting `evidence` preserves the current thread
evidence. `append` therefore cannot silently erase the existing five gaps or six prescriptions;
use `replace` only when sending the full intended replacement list. The same rule applies to
`assetInspections[]` and `runtimeChecks[]`; all `frameIds` must resolve to frames in the same
manifest, and stable IDs are upserted on append. `assetInspections[].numericContract` is the
static score/threshold/hard-blocker/draw-call/bounds layer; it never changes `visualRuntime` or
`reviewStatus`.
Each linked inspection also has `origin: "file" | "procedural" | "runtime-generated"`; non-file
origins require `provenance.sourceRef` plus optional source commit, generator, and recipe id. A
procedural crop or NPC can therefore be reviewed against its source module and shipped frame
without inventing a GLB byte result.

The displayed `score: 100` / `hardBlockerCount: 0` is a declared static policy contract. INFO
findings such as missing normals, non-unit scale, empty nodes, missing UVs, or textureCount 0 may
still be visible observations and can require renderer review. It is not a visual quality PASS,
engine import PASS, or player-facing approval. Current HF M98 near observations include
cultivator `16196 triangles / 42 draw calls`, processing `24936 / 78`, seeder `11318 / 75`, and
tractor `30188 / 88`, all with textureCount 0; HF crops/vegetation/NPCs are procedural runtime
surfaces rather than standalone GLBs and must use provenance-linked frame evidence.

The same bundle shape is also available through the authenticated app API:

```json
POST /api/assetops/inspect
{
  "schema": "clunk.asset-inspection-request.v1",
  "fileName": "tractor.compact.m1.glb",
  "bytesBase64": "<BASE64_BYTES>",
  "targetProfileId": "harvest-frontier-web-three",
  "assetKind": "3d-model",
  "runId": "HF-M96-tractor-r01"
}
```

It requires the authenticated workspace context, returns `clunk.asset-inspection-response.v1`,
and does not persist raw bytes. The remote MCP uses the same request shape with the issued Bearer
key. Store the returned evidence or its `inputHash` in a collaboration manifest when linking a
shipped frame.

For Sprite Atlas and Spine projects, use the bounded multi-file request contract. This is the
authenticated bundle path for a Spine JSON + atlas + PNG project. The same shape is accepted by
the Clunk-owned remote HTTP MCP when sent with a workspace Bearer key:

```json
POST /api/assetops/inspect
{
  "schema": "clunk.asset-inspection-request.v2",
  "entryFileName": "spine/character.json",
  "files": [
    { "fileName": "spine/character.json", "role": "entry", "bytesBase64": "<SPINE_JSON>" },
    { "fileName": "spine/character.atlas", "role": "atlas", "relatesTo": ["spine/character.json"], "bytesBase64": "<ATLAS_TEXT>" },
    { "fileName": "spine/body.png", "role": "page", "relatesTo": ["spine/character.atlas"], "bytesBase64": "<PNG_BYTES>" }
  ],
  "targetProfileId": "harvest-frontier-web-three",
  "assetKind": "spine-project",
  "runId": "HF-M99-spine-r01"
}
```

The v2 response is `clunk.asset-inspection-response.v2` and adds a non-persistent `bundle` summary:
`entryFileName`, `fileCount`, `totalBytes`, and each member's `fileName`, byte count, SHA-256,
optional `role`, and validated `relatesTo` file names. `role` is one of `entry|project|atlas|page|texture|skeleton|animation|buffer|sidecar|unknown`;
relations must point to another submitted file. This makes an atlas+page or Spine JSON+atlas+texture
relationship auditable without persisting raw bytes.
Names are safe relative slash paths only; duplicate names, missing entries, malformed base64,
more than 256 files, or decoded aggregate bytes over 64 MiB are rejected. The legacy v1
`fileName` + `bytesBase64` request remains supported. A multi-file structural PASS only proves
the references were reopened from supplied bytes; missing engine import/runtime remains
`ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, and it never changes `visualRuntime`, `reviewStatus`, or `playerFacing`.

For UI readability, `clunk.ui-readability.v1` also preserves optional `renderContext` metadata:
`css.sha256`, viewport/dpr, font family/size/weight/lineHeight, renderer/kernel, and
`metadataCompleteness` (`COMPLETE` or `PARTIAL`). `criteria.deltaE76[]` records the per-group
`meanDeltaE76` metric and threshold. The raster contract remains `PASS|FAIL|UNAVAILABLE` with
exit `0|2|4`; it never promotes engine/runtime or player-facing readiness.

The local CLI validates the same envelope before an authenticated POST and can produce the
same append/replace result for CI:

```text
npm.cmd run collaboration:frame-manifest -- validate --input hf-frame-manifest.json --format json
npm.cmd run collaboration:frame-manifest -- merge --current stored.json --incoming next.json --mode append --format json
```
Both commands print normalized JSON and return exit `0` for valid evidence or exit `2` for
malformed evidence/invalid cross-run append. The dashboard form exposes the same choice as
`replace · full snapshot` and `append · keep existing IDs`.

Frame comparisons use `clunk.frame-comparison.v1` nested inside the compatible
`clunk.frame-manifest.v1` envelope. Each pair references `beforeFrameId` and `afterFrameId`;
both frames must be shipped-path captures with SHA-256, bytes, renderer, viewport, console,
camera pose, `cameraPoseHash`, and `sourceTreeHash`. The normalizer rejects each mismatch
explicitly as `cameraPoseHash mismatch`, `cameraPose mismatch`, `renderer mismatch`,
`viewport mismatch`, or `sourceTreeHash mismatch`. `append` preserves and stable-id-upserts
comparison pairs; `replace` replaces the complete comparison snapshot.

Every `sceneGaps[]` entry may carry a per-gap `closeout` with `status` `OPEN|CLOSED|REOPENED|NOT_EVALUATED`,
`owner`, `humanDecision`, `comparisonId`, and evidence. `CLOSED` requires a PASS comparison
decision plus after-frame evidence, but a closed gap never promotes the manifest's
`visualRuntime=GAP` or `playerFacing=NOT_EVALUATED`. Procedural and runtime-generated asset
inspections always normalize to `playerFacing: NOT_EVALUATED`; a linked real frame is necessary
but not sufficient, and no numeric score can become a player-facing PASS.

The player-facing scene contract is a separate evidence check:
`npm.cmd run collaboration:frame-manifest -- scene-review --input hf-frame-manifest.json --format json`.
For CI that must preserve the child process's exact exit code on Windows, use
`npm.cmd exec -- tsx scripts/frame-manifest-cli.ts scene-review --input hf-frame-manifest.json --format json`.
It returns `clunk.player-facing-scene-review.v1` with `PASS_WITH_FOLLOW_UP`, `NO_GO`, or
`UNAVAILABLE`; exit codes are `0`, `2`, and `4` respectively. Each enriched `sceneGaps[]` item
must carry severity, `ownership`, affected scene or asset IDs, `nextStep`, and linked evidence
`path`/SHA-256. `linkedAssets[].numericContract.score` may still be `100`, while
`ownership: asset|runtime|unknown` and `runtimeUsage: USED_IN_FRAME|NOT_USED_IN_FRAME|UNKNOWN`
remain explicit. `textureCount: 0` is not itself a defect. This command is an evidence/metadata
gate only: `visualRuntime` stays `GAP`, `playerFacing` stays `NOT_EVALUATED`, and
`humanReview` stays `PENDING`; no headless result is visual approval.

The `harvest-frontier-web-three` target applies semantic rule
`harvest-frontier-runtime-v1` inside the unified AssetOps pipeline. It checks named runtime
root, pivot, attachment socket, collider proxy and `EXT_meshopt_compression` as structural or
policy evidence. Semantic PASS does not prove Three.js import/runtime, procedural crop,
vegetation or NPC quality, shipped-camera composition, or human visual approval. Missing
engine runners remain `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`; Clunk does not optimize HF GLBs without
explicit approval.

belong to procedural/material runtime authoring; ownership and runtime usage must remain
explicit in linked evidence, and a shipped WebGPU/WebGL2 frame plus human review is still
required for player-facing approval.

## Safety boundaries

- The input file is never overwritten. Optimization always writes a separate artifact.
- Allowlisted operations only: `prune-empty-nodes`, `dedupe-materials`, `clean-metadata`,
  `repack`. The first, second and fourth are lossless; `clean-metadata` is metadata only.
- Not applied automatically in v1: mesh simplification, texture re-encoding, Draco or Meshopt
  compression, quantization, animation and skin edits, unknown extension rewrites.
- An asset is only reported ready after parse, policy, score, fresh re-inspection of the output
  bytes, blocker review, and reopening the downloaded artifact all pass.

## Local first

The web inspector parses asset bytes in the browser. Only metadata, hashes and results are
stored server side. Original asset bytes are not uploaded automatically, and artifact storage
is deliberately disabled during the pilot.

## Surfaces

Web inspector (`app/app`), CLI (`scripts/clunk-cli.ts`), MCP server (`integrations/mcp`),
VS Code extension (`integrations/vscode`). All four call the same Core contract and record the
same identifiers.

## Custom profiles

Project-specific inspection profiles are supported as JSON definitions: CLI `--profile-file <path.json>` and MCP tool argument `profileFile`. See docs/custom-profiles.ko.md and examples/profiles/harvest-frontier.example.json. Built-in profiles (web/mobile/pc) remain byte-identical. The web inspector accepts the same profile JSON for local-only inspection (no save, no credit).

## Asset Studio and authoring pipeline

Asset Studio (`/studio`) is the authenticated authoring-to-runtime surface for both 2D and 3D:
`2d-image` (Sprite/Frame), `sprite-atlas` (Atlas + regions), `spine-project` (Spine JSON +
atlas + texture), `animation-clip` (glTF motion), and `3d-model` (GLB/GLTF). The same workflow
is `CREATE -> INSPECT -> ATTACH -> REVIEW`.

Verified local authoring commands write separate output artifacts and reopen them through the
same target profile:

```text
npm.cmd run asset:author -- --asset-kind 2d-image --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --recipe-id sprite-sheet-factory-v1 --recipe-version 1.0.0 --output-directory output/generated
npm.cmd run asset:author -- --asset-kind sprite-atlas --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --recipe-id sprite-atlas-factory-v1 --recipe-version 1.0.0 --output-directory output/generated
npm.cmd run asset:author -- --asset-kind spine-project --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --recipe-id spine-json-factory-v1 --recipe-version 1.0.0 --output-directory output/generated
npm.cmd run asset:author -- --asset-kind animation-clip --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --recipe-id threejs-animation-factory-v1 --recipe-version 1.0.0 --output-directory output/generated
npm.cmd run asset:generate -- --factory examples/generated/windmill.factory.mjs --target-profile harvest-frontier-web-three --recipe-id threejs-factory-v1 --recipe-version 1.0.0 --output-directory output/generated
```

The 2D/Spine authoring adapters emit real PNG/atlas/JSON bytes and a generation sidecar with
source/recipe/output hashes; the output is then inspected by AssetOps. Binary Spine `.skel`
parsing, licensed Spine export parity, and Godot/Unity/Unreal/mobile import or playback remain
`UNAVAILABLE` until a real adapter/runner is supplied. Procedural authored output is not a
player-facing approval. Structural PASS, engine import/runtime, shipped frame evidence, and
human visual review remain independent.

Local stdio MCP additionally exposes `clunk_asset_author` with the same assetKind,
targetProfileId, recipeId, outputDirectory, and optional factoryPath fields. It can write only to
the caller's local output directory and always uses a separate output plus reopen evidence. The
remote HTTPS MCP intentionally does not expose this write-capable tool: upload the resulting
bundle through `clunk_asset_inspect` or `clunk_asset_inspection_evidence` instead. A generated
bundle can be structurally PASS while runtime status is `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE` and
playerFacing remains `NOT_EVALUATED`.

## Pixi sprite-sheet review

Clunk exposes `clunk.sprite-sheet-review.v1` for the `yeongheo-pixi-2d` target profile. The contract
keeps `CONTRACT_FIXTURE` and `PLAYER_FACING_CAPTURE` separate and covers grid/cell,
direction/state/fps/loop/holdLast, pivot/hitbox, opaque-bottom, duplicate and motion delta,
clipping, alpha spill, border, silhouette, and runtime-size checks. A structural or pixel PASS is
not a player-facing or human PASS.

For exact RGBA evidence, run the local CLI against the declared sheet bytes:

```text
npm.cmd run asset:sprite-audit -- validate --input manifest.json --format json --required
```

Exit semantics: exit 0 PASS, exit 2 policy or quality FAIL, and exit 4 UNAVAILABLE (including
missing local bytes or a required review that cannot be completed). The authenticated HTTP API and
remote MCP use `DECLARED_METADATA_ONLY`: they never dereference a local path or pretend to rehash
it. Use local CLI/MCP stdio for `LOCAL_CLI_BYTE_REHASH`; keep `visualRuntime`, `playerFacing`, and
`humanDecision` independent.
